edges.description: The one driver sits in a tumour that then differentiates two ways at once. No cached source demonstrates that the mutation causes the divergence; what they show is that both components share the tumour and that it carries the mutation.

The skeletal muscle arm of the divergence is what the rhabdomyosarcomatous half of the tumour is. The edge is constitutive rather than sequential: the differentiation programme and the component it produces are the same event described at two scales, and no cited source times one against the other.
The neural crest arm of the same divergence. Unlike the muscle arm it does not settle on one cell type, which is why the component it produces is recorded as a spectrum rather than as a diagnosis.
The two differentiating populations make up the mass that presents.

The tumour is what the child presents with, and where it sits is set by where the neural crest went. This is the entry's only edge into the clinical layer, which is a statement about the literature rather than about the disease: none of the cited sources is a study of presentation.
edges.target: Mass at a Neural Crest Migration Site

nodes.description: The tumour that presents. The two series this node's locations are bound from both put the pelvic and genitourinary region first, to different degrees: all but one of seven in the genomic series, and 8 of 17 - a plurality, not a majority - in the larger one. A third cited series puts the head and neck first at 45.6%, which is why the phenotype row downstream of this node is bound site-agnostically and this node's locations should be read as the commonest sites rather than the only ones.

nodes.description: The defining event: one tumour running a skeletal muscle programme and a neural crest programme at once. The mesenchymal component was embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma in 16 of 17 tumours in the larger cached series and in all seven of the genomic one. The neuroectodermal component is not one thing - the same series found neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma or ganglion cells, composite ganglioneuroblastoma and Schwann cell differentiation across its cases.

evidence.snippet: The neuroectodermal component encompassed the spectrum of neural crest differentiation, including neuroblastoma in 12 cases, ganglioneuroma/ganglion cells in 2 cases, composite ganglioneuroblastoma in 1 case, and Schwann cell differentiation in 2 cases.

nodes.description: An activating hotspot mutation in HRAS, found in six of the seven tumours of the cached genomic series. Four carried p.G13R and two p.Q61L. Transcriptome sequencing of its two index cases found no fusion gene, and instead recurrent HRAS and PTPRD hotspot mutations in both; what singled HRAS out was the screen across the remaining five tumours, in which no further PTPRD or FBXW7 mutation appeared.

evidence.snippet: In total, 6 of 7 (86%) MEMs harbored HRAS mutations, 4 with p.G13R mutation and 2 with p.Q61L.

meta.frequency: the commonest alteration in one series and an uncommon one in the other

nodes.description: The presenting finding. The tumour arises along the paths the neural crest takes, so the site varies widely; the pelvis and perineum are the commonest in one series and the head and neck in another, and the pelvic or genitourinary region in a third. Every HPO mass term names a body site - abdominal, pelvic, mediastinal and so on - and those are siblings of one another rather than a general and a specific form of one thing, so binding any of them would assert a site this tumour does not keep to. The binding is therefore to soft tissue neoplasm, which two cited sources state in terms and which carries no site.

evidence.reference_title: Malignant Ectomesenchymoma: Series Analysis of a Histologically and Genetically Heterogeneous Tumor.
evidence.snippet: Ectomesenchymoma manifests in various sites given the wide migration of neural crest cells during development, though the pelvis/perineum is most often involved.

evidence.reference_title: A single-center retrospective study of malignant ectomesenchymoma in children.
evidence.snippet: The most commonly affected sites were the head and neck (45.6%), followed by the limbs (27.2%) and the pelvis/abdomen (27.2%).

evidence.reference_title: Malignant ectomesenchymoma in children: The European pediatric Soft tissue sarcoma Study Group experience.
evidence.snippet: Malignant ectomesenchymoma (MEM) is an extremely rare soft tissue tumor typical of young children, currently included in the category of skeletal muscle malignancies and characterized by a neuroblastic component.

evidence.reference_title: Somatic and mosaic HRAS mutations in pediatric malignant ectomesenchymoma.
evidence.snippet: Malignant ectomesenchymoma (ME), a rare tumor of soft tissues, has a neuroectodermal component of neuroblasts and/or ganglion cells, and a mesenchymal component mostly often represented by rhabdomyoblasts.

nodes.description: The neuroectodermal half: most often a neuroblastic tumour, but spanning the range of neural-crest differentiation, from neuroblastoma through ganglioneuroma and ganglion cells to Schwann-cell differentiation. The binding is at the neuroblastic parent term, which is the commonest form and the only part of that range HPO subsumes under one concept; the ganglionic and Schwann-cell forms fall outside it and are carried by the row's description and by the cell types on the upstream pathophysiology node. HPO files this term under malignant neoplasm of the central nervous system, which this tumour is not - a closure query over that parent will pick this entry up wrongly, and the entry has no better anchor to offer.

evidence.reference_title: [Clinicopathological and molecular genetic characteristics of embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma with divergent neuroectodermal differentiation: an analysis of 17 cases].
evidence.snippet: The neuroectodermal component encompassed the spectrum of neural crest differentiation, including neuroblastoma in 12 cases, ganglioneuroma/ganglion cells in 2 cases, composite ganglioneuroblastoma in 1 case, and Schwann cell differentiation in 2 cases.

nodes.description: Radiotherapy was given to four of the ten patients in the European series. The Chinese single-centre series reports a lower relapse rate in its irradiated group, which is the only comparative result in any cited source on local treatment. Its own abstract gives two irreconcilable counts for how many of its children were irradiated - four of the nine who had surgery in one sentence, six in the relapse comparison - and the entry quotes both rather than choosing between them.

evidence.reference_title: A single-center retrospective study of malignant ectomesenchymoma in children.
evidence.snippet: Children who received both radiotherapy and chemotherapy had a significantly lower relapse rate compared to those treated with chemotherapy alone (2/6 vs. 5/5, P = 0.046).

evidence.reference_title: Malignant ectomesenchymoma in children: The European pediatric Soft tissue sarcoma Study Group experience.
evidence.snippet: All patients received chemotherapy according to rhabdomyosarcoma strategy, four had radiotherapy.

nodes.description: The mesenchymal half of the tumour, rhabdomyosarcoma in every case of the series cited here, most often embryonal. It is a component of the tumour rather than a separate presenting complaint, which is why it is recorded as a phenotype of the mass rather than as a symptom.

evidence.reference_title: Malignant Ectomesenchymoma: Series Analysis of a Histologically and Genetically Heterogeneous Tumor.
evidence.snippet: Mesenchymal elements, represented by rhabdomyosarcoma in all instances, were the dominant component in the majority of cases (5/6).

nodes.description: Gross resection of the primary tumour. The German cooperative-group series describes it as the local treatment its patients received alongside chemotherapy; the European series' cached abstract names chemotherapy and radiotherapy and does not mention surgery at all. No cited source isolates resection's effect: the series report what was done and what happened, not a comparison against not resecting.

evidence.reference_title: Malignant ectomesenchymoma in children and adolescents: report from the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe (CWS).
evidence.snippet: The tumors of 4/5 patients with localized MEM were at least grossly resected at best surgery; the patient without gross resection was additionally irradiated.
